body:
REMOTE RUNNERS AND PER-HOST CARGO LIMITS (rev 7, 2026-10-30 about 00:22Z; Engram::Fable and Termal::Fable2 concurred, #5332–#5334). Older stage and deferral detail is in rev 6. A working operating agreement, not an authority rule.
SOURCES:
- Greg, Engram Advisor #2314, 00:14:53Z, verbatim: „Greg: możemy mieć więcej równoległych Cargo, jeśli wyniesiemy runnery testów na inne maszyny. Proszę uzgodnić z TermAl limity per host wg pomiarów CPU/RAM/dysku i izolacji target/worktree, zamiast stosować jeden slot Central jako limit całego systemu. Zachować wymagania poszczególnych gateów.”
- Greg, Engram Advisor #2311: „Mac jako preferowany runner TermAl, a DL560 jako preferowany runner Engram … sprawdzić realne czasy Engram na DL560 i zachować wymagane testy platformowe.”
- The DL560 deferral was lifted by Greg (TermAl Advisor #2618, relayed by Fable2 #5317).
- Greg (2026-10-29): use TermAl test-runs and launcher completion, not a model operator reading test output.
SPLIT: DL560 is Engram's preferred runner and the Mac is TermAl's. Each side may use the other's host when that host's own lane is idle, telling the other first. Windows-only tests stay on Windows. Engram::Fable hands out the Engram lanes on DL560; Fable2 hands out the TermAl lanes, the Mac, Windows B and Central Cargo.
AGREED TEXT:
1. SLOTS PER HOST, not one system-wide slot. Each host has its own Cargo limit.
2. ISOLATION for every job on every host:
   - a separate runner clone per project per host, push URL disabled;
   - a fresh detached worktree per job, with its own target directory (never a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR) and its own throwaway home under the worktree's ignored target/;
   - `env -i`, `ulimit -n 16384`, no live store and no real ENGRAM_HOME;
   - at least 60 GB disk free at launch beyond what's already reserved;
   - launcher fingerprints match before and after, and `git status --porcelain` is empty.
   Inputs: a patch accepted only when HEAD == BASE and write-tree == TREE, or a test ref for a merge-ready input.
3. DL560 (144 cores, about 247 GB RAM, about 966 GB disk): start at 2 concurrent jobs (1 Engram + 1 TermAl). Raise 2→4→… only while the measured overlap slowdown against the solo baseline stays under about 20% and RAM stays under about 70%. Heavy Engram jobs (Nmax, repeat-stress) run alone or with at most one light job. Solo baselines: TermAl 30m38s at ce2487a8; Engram clean master 83093646, pending.
4. TermAl-scheduled hosts:
   - MAC (M1, 8 cores, 16 GB RAM, about 78 GB free): 1 job at a time; remove each worktree as soon as its evidence is recorded.
   - WINDOWS B (24 threads, 64 GB RAM, 511 GB disk): either 1 full gate or 2 focused jobs, with at least 25 GiB free commit at each launch.
   - CENTRAL: unchanged at 1, quiet for full and whole-bin runs, until it is measured again.
5. GATES UNCHANGED: landing gates stay where the current rules put them. Remote runs are author evidence. A remote FULL gate counts for landing only through the project's test-ref route plus an imported check record bound to the tree id (Fable2 plans this for Windows landing gates on Windows B). A Windows-only change needs a Windows gate.
COMPLETION ROUTE over SSH (Fable2 #5336):
- No real TermAl identity exists over SSH. DL560's TermAl CLI talks only to DL560's own host, so never invent a TERMAL_SESSION_ID, and never use nohup.
- The operator runs the launcher in the FOREGROUND inside ONE ssh command, started from its own background shell on Central, so that the command's exit wakes it.
- Fable2 sets a one-shot backstop wake at the expected end plus about 10 min, so the operator sends Fable2 START with the expected end time.
- On whichever wake comes first, read `summary` once. No polling and no rerun.
- First proof: Opus3's run ending about 00:40Z.
ENGRAM LANE: an Engram session operates it (first: Coder 11334). Clone ~/github/Engram-runner (never Greg's ~/github/Engram). Results go to Fable and Fable2, labelled "measurement; not a landing gate" or "Linux author evidence; not a landing gate"; then remove the worktree.

PROOF (Fable2 #5339, 00:22:52Z): the background-ssh exit wake WORKS on the current host build for Claude operators. Opus3's DL560 run ended at 00:21:43Z and its END reached Fable2 at 00:22:09Z, with no polling and no backstop needed. A Codex operator (Coder 11334) keeps its exec session alive and relies on Fable2's backstop wake.

CORRECTION TO POINT 5 (Fable2 #5340, 00:23:33Z): the parenthetical "Fable2 plans this for Windows landing gates on Windows B" is WITHDRAWN. Merger2's read-only audit found no typed remote check importer. The earlier WINB and Mac "imports" were evidence archives, and Central supplied the recognized landing gate (TermAl procedure remote-test-ref-gates-evidence-only r4). So today landing gates stay on Central, and Windows B, the Mac and DL560 are author-evidence lanes only. The rest of point 5 stands.



CODEX OPERATOR BACKSTOP (2026-10-30, Fable2 #5412 after the test-6c60bff3 idle gap): a Codex foreground SSH exec gives no completion wake. So for each Codex-operated remote run, the operator's START names the backstop time T. Fable2 creates a DEDICATED one-shot at T and echoes "SET for T (job id)", and the operator launches only after that echo. A general periodic backstop does not count. The structural gap belongs to TermAl w-2f30's automatic pull; no new item.

UNIX GATE CAVEAT (rev 11, 2026-10-30 17:30Z; Fable2 #5476 for DL560, extended to the Mac by Engram::Fable): until Engram w-e7ba3da8e36c lands, an Engram full gate on DL560 or the Mac can fail on diagnostics::mcp::tests::routing::actual_rmcp_cancellation_releases_slots_and_quarantine_overflow_fails_closed. That happened on DL560 in test-9b95e2ed. The mechanism, reproduced by RED test-8c1a56c2: a flock lock stays held through an open file description inherited by a forked child. It is timing-dependent. Rely on Central or Windows B for Engram landing gates until then. If a Unix gate does fail on that test, record it on w-e7ba; it is a known defect, not a reason to retry.

ENGRAM LANE SSH ROUTE (rev 12, 2026-10-31 02:45Z, confirmed by Engram::Fable for Engram::Opus #3630): `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes dl560`, using this Windows host's configured ~/.ssh/config entry "Host dl560 / HostName dl560 / User greg / IdentityFile C:/Users/grzeg/.ssh/termal_dl560 / IdentitiesOnly yes". The runner clone is ~/github/Engram-runner on DL560 (push disabled). Patch route: apply the contribution on the stated master commit, require `git write-tree` to equal the reviewed tree, then run the launcher (focused or full) with env -i, the ulimit above, and its own target and home. Evidence only, unless the test-ref rules make it a landing gate. A filtered test must show it actually executed (at least 1 test by name).

REV 13 (2026-10-31 07:10Z): the UNIX GATE CAVEAT is RETIRED. w-e7ba (the diagnostics flock fork-inheritance fix) landed in master dcbff8c7 on 2026-10-31 05:31Z, so an Engram full gate on DL560 or the Mac no longer carries that known failure. Option B (candidate commits) is in force since 40ca0bd0, so a candidate commit is the natural test-ref input. Engram landing gates may use DL560, the Mac or Windows B through the AGENTS.md test-ref route, with the run facts recorded by the integration owner. Proposed for A's gate to Merger3 (#585).

REV 14 (2026-10-31 07:25Z, Engram::Architect3 #201, after Greg asked why SSH is used): the manual foreground SSH plus backstop route is a FALLBACK for a concrete missing or broken step in the federated handoff (mailbox → native remote root → that host's own test-runs → completion/wake). It is not the permanent runner workflow. The SSH tunnel itself is fine, and the native-mailbox relay already reaches host-qualified roots (the directory lists DL560 roots). Don't call a native root absent only from allocatedSessions=0 or null telemetry. When the native route works, the agent only submits the input and reads terminal metadata; TermAl owns the run, logs and wake. The owner item and the exact gap were asked of Fable2 (#5600).
